Explicitly prioritizes remaining work by expected gain: lists documentHighlight (66.3%, 3506 failures), references (37.1%, 5718 failures), prepareCallHierarchy (60.3%, 4323 failures), and picks references 'because it's the biggest gain' — weighing case counts, not just percentages.

Recognizes circular/unwinnable debugging on overloaded-method distinction ('Hard without full type inference. Let me skip this for now') and explicitly steps back to higher-value work — classic thrash-avoidance.

Continuously tracks both the global aggregate (21%->77%->89%->95.23%) and per-method 100%-completion milestones (folding, typeDefinition, definition, codeLens), never losing sight of the all-tests-pass target while working local failures.

reasoning: Across 250 steps the agent kept a live per-method/per-file pass ledger, re-scored after nearly every change, and caught regressions the moment the count moved the wrong way — then reverted (steps 99,125,140,221,237). It prioritized remaining work by expected gain using failure counts (step 116) and explicitly abandoned an unwinnable case rather than circling it (step 1935), all while tracking the global percentage toward all-tests-pass. This matches the level-8 anchor fully and most of level-10 (expected-gain prioritization, catching thrash and stepping back); it falls just short of a perfect 10 because the ledger is reconstructed by re-running the scorer rather than persisted, and there was brief churn on the references/overload cases (steps 217-225) before recovery.
